_comment: Linux x86_64 native self-build perf baseline. Captured 2026-05-06 (RFC-0063 Phase 1.3, R10-D3 closure); v1.0.1 update 2026-05-09 (audit-pass-1 closure); D1 RSS split schema added 2026-05-10. Companion to tools/perf_baseline.json (Windows). Pass via tools/check_perf_regression.sh --baseline tools/perf_baseline_linux.json on Linux runners. Update only after a measured intentional improvement; never to absorb a regression.
_d1_split_note: 2026-05-10 D1 (Linux RSS split): added cold_compiler_peak_memory_mb / hot_compiler_peak_memory_mb / cold_max_allowed_compiler_memory_mb / hot_max_allowed_compiler_memory_mb so the POSIX perf gate enforces the same four-ceiling contract as Windows. tools/check_perf_regression.sh --doctor now FAILs without these fields. The compiler-only peak values below are PLACEHOLDERS (mirrored from process-tree until a native Linux runner re-measures and re-locks under Step 7 of docs/LINUX_PERF_AND_RELEASE_HANDOFF_2026-05-10.md). The compiler-only ceilings are set to the process-tree ceiling for now (a safe over-approximation because compiler-only RSS <= process-tree RSS by construction); tighten them on the first native-Linux measurement run.
_v1_0_1_audit_note: v1.0.1 (2026-05-09) cold path measured 28-30 s due to audit-pass-1 added correctness checks (Lane 4 lex hardening for NUL/CR/numeric-literal hygiene, Lane 1 type-system additions, Lane 2 G-1..G-11 ownership analyses, Lane 6 RT-attribute scanner). The hot path improved 14x (0.033 s vs 0.47 s baseline) thanks to integrator-side cache-check sequencing + early raw-source fast path. Cold-path optimization (move per-byte loops in lex/ownership/emit to C runtime helpers) is the v1.0.2 perf deliverable. The cold ceiling below is INTENTIONALLY relaxed for v1.0.1 to avoid suppressing correctness-required audit fixes; v1.0.2 must close the gap back toward the v0.8.323 baseline.

host.binary: bin/nucleor (ELF 64-bit LSB pie, x86-64-v1, -O3+LTO, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0)

_anti_compound_rule: Each Linux ship must come in at or below the ceilings above. Drift > 5% but < 10% requires investigation before shipping; never bump to absorb a regression. v1.0.1 is the ONE TIME exception per the audit-pass-1 note above; v1.0.2 must demonstrate cold-path improvement (target <=15 s as a milestone toward the v0.8.323 9.05 s baseline).

_history.note: First-ever native Linux baseline (R10-D3 closure). Cold is ~2.4x the v0.8.317 Windows baseline (3.73s); hot is ~1.8x (0.26s). Gap is concentrated in the cold path — likely fopen / fork / exec / clang invocation overhead on Linux's standard glibc + ld-linux setup vs the v0.8.317 Windows tooling. Earmarked for RFC-0063 Phase 4 (PGO + LTO + per-arch SIMD). The hot-path delta is small enough that Linux production is viable today; the cold-path gap is the v1.0 perf target.

_history.samples: 1 cold + 1 hot (single-run estimate; precise sampling deferred to v1.0.2 perf-debt sprint)
_history.note: v1.0.1 audit-pass-1 closure. Hot path 14x improvement (0.034 s) thanks to integrator-side cache-check sequencing + early raw-source cache fast path. Cold path 3.1x slowdown vs v0.8.323 baseline due to audit-added correctness checks: Lane 4 LEX-001 byte rejection + numeric-literal hygiene checks (lex 8s vs ~3s pre-audit), Lane 2 G-1..G-11 ownership analyses (ownership 3.4s), Lane 6 RT scanner (~500ms), preflight + audit-pass scanners gated to non-self-host but still scan adopter source. Cold-path closeback to <=15s is the explicit v1.0.2 perf deliverable; the path involves moving lex's per-byte loops + ownership's per-fn walks to C runtime helpers (target: 50-100x reduction on those passes) and a more aggressive load_resolved_source_bundle module-graph cache for non-self-host sources.
